title: DPF Regeneration Required
fullDescription:
Kubota M-series, MX-series, and L-series Tier 4 Final tractors monitor DPF soot. P3000 sets when soot loading exceeds passive regen capability and the operator must trigger a parked regen.

Ignoring P3000 leads to higher-tier faults requiring dealer service.

fixSteps.title: Initiate parked regen
fixSteps.instruction: Park, neutral, set brake, activate regen switch. 25-40 minutes.

whenToCallPro: Only if regen will not start.

faq.a: Yes - drivers who suppress regen build soot to higher fault levels.

title: DPF Efficiency Below Threshold
fullDescription: Indicates a failed DPF substrate, often after a runaway regen or attempted delete. Replacement is the typical fix.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DPF visually
fixSteps.instruction: Borescope through O2 sensor port for cracks/missing cells.

fixSteps.title: Replace DPF
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM unit, reset DPF service via Diagmaster.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low
fullDescription:
Kubota V-series common rail engines. Plugged filters, contaminated fuel, and air ingress are top causes on tractors.

Replace filters and bleed system.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuel filters
fixSteps.instruction: Primary water separator and main filter.

fixSteps.title: Bleed system
fixSteps.instruction: Hand-prime and crank to purge air.

faq.a: Bulk farm tanks accumulate water - drain water separator weekly.

title: Turbocharger Underboost
fullDescription: Kubota turbo failures often result from oil starvation (clogged feed line) or charge air leak. Inspect intercooler boots first - they crack near the clamps.

fixSteps.title: Inspect charge air boots
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cracks, especially at clamp swedge points.

fixSteps.title: Test turbo wheel play
fixSteps.instruction: Pull intake, wiggle wheel - excess axial play means turbo replacement.

faq.a: Less effective on Kubota - typically a hard mechanical issue.

title: EGR Insufficient Flow
shortDescription: EGR system not flowing as commanded.
fullDescription: Carbon-stuck EGR valve is the leading Kubota EGR fault. Clean or replace valve. Check cooler if heavily plugged.

fixSteps.title: Clean EGR valve
fixSteps.instruction: Remove, soak in carb cleaner, scrub.

faq.a: Every 1500-2000 hours on heavy idle duty.

title: ECU Internal Performance Failure
fullDescription:
Internal ECU error. Common after water intrusion to the ECU enclosure or loose grounds.

Check grounds first, then dealer reflash or ECU replacement.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ECU mount and connector
fixSteps.instruction: Look for moisture or corroded pins.

faq.a: Yes - never spray ECU connectors directly.

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit
fullDescription: Kubota M and MX series CKP sensor failure causes no-start or stalling when hot. Sensor is inexpensive.

fixSteps.title: Resistance check sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to spec, replace if open.

title: Cooling Fan Control Circuit
fullDescription: Kubota MX/M series viscous fan clutch electronic control fault. Often a failed solenoid.

faq.a: Most Kubota fans are belt-driven via clutch, not electric.

title: DEF Quality Sensor Fault
shortDescription: DEF quality sensor signal out of range.
fullDescription: Kubota M7 SCR-equipped tractors monitor DEF quality. P1000 indicates the quality sensor is faulty or DEF is contaminated.
whenToCallPro: If sensor and refill don't resolve.

title: Engine Protection Derate Active
shortDescription: Engine in protection mode from upstream fault.
fullDescription: Kubota generic protection trigger. Look at parallel codes for root cause.

faq.a: Yes, after root cause is fixed.
